messages:
alex: heads-up — after the base-image + nvidia-container-toolkit bump in the gpu-image pipeline, a subset of containers are failing at launch with libcuda/driver missing errors. started ~06:12 UTC.

tess: can you paste the exact error? which tag did we push? :eyes:

alex: error from model-server container: \"error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory\". Image tag: gpu-base:2026-03-18-toolkit1.13

sanjay: seeing same on 3 nodes in us-west1 and 2 in eu-central (k8s nodes on kernel 6.1 and 5.15 mix). Containers on older kernel nodes still okay. Suspect mount propagation/overlay + rshared behavior changed in toolkit hook.

jen: @oncall can we cordon affected nodes and route traffic to dedicated fallback pool? Want to avoid model errors hitting prod.

infra-bot: deploy.pipeline gpu-image build 8472 failed on Canary node (node-uw-03) — reverting to previous tag in progress.

dana: quick mitigation: for affected tenants we can roll back the gpu-base image to the prior tag (toolkit 1.11) and that fixes the lib load. Long term we need a fix in the toolkit packaging to use rbind + make-rshared on the host-side bind so libnvidia libs appear inside overlayfs mounts.

mike: NCCL tests also flaking — process startup hits the same ldopen failure causing fallback codepaths and huge perf regression in 4-node perf runs. This isn't only a single-model issue.

ryan: temporary workaround that worked on a lab node: start container with --volume /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/host-lib:ro --env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH and set NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all. Ugly but confirms libs are present on host and it's a propagation/mounts issue, not the driver itself.

tess: can you attach kubelet logs and the container runtime (containerd) error for one failing pod? need to confirm if the hook is failing or if overlay blocked the bind.

alex: pasted minimal logs:
```
Mar 18 06:12:34 node-uw-03 containerd[1234]: time=\"2026-03-18T06:12:34Z\" level=error msg=\"failed to start containerd task\" error=\"OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: error mounting \\\"/usr/lib/nvidia\\\" to rootfs at \\\"/usr/local/nvidia\\\": mount failed: exit status 32: mounting denied by mount propagation\\\"\"
```

sanjay: that matches the rshared -> rprivate regression we've seen in some kernel/toolkit combinations. When the toolkit uses an rbind but the host mount is rprivate overlay can hide it.

jen: plan: 1) cordon affected nodes (in progress), 2) rollback image in pipeline (in progress), 3) patch node bootstrap to set /usr/lib/nvidia mounts as rshared on next reboot, 4) follow-up with distro / toolkit maintainers for upstream fix. Approving emergency rollout to rollback tag now.

dana: note for private customers with on-prem images — we'll need to push a hotfix image that copies necessary nvidia libs into the container at build time (avoid host bind), since some air-gapped environments can't change host mount propagation.

mike: for load testing, I'll queue a NCCL sanity job against the rollback tag and the rshared patch nodes to validate end-to-end before uncordoning.

ryan: after rollback, keep an eye on autoscaler — we had a spike in Pending pods while we drained nodes. Might need temporary burst capacity to avoid throttling admission.

alex: filed infra ticket INFRA-1298 with the kernel/toolkit matrix, attached logs and node list. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-platform. Will follow up with a postmortem once we have root cause. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: ticket INFRA-1298 created by alex — severity P2 — linked to deploy.pipeline build 8472.

tess: thanks — keep updates here. If anyone finds a smaller repro (single docker run) post it, we should get a test that fails in CI to prevent future rollouts.

alex: will add a repro recipe and a small harness that simulates overlay/rshared combos. Closing channel for action items; updates into INFRA-1298.
